name: Olympic Games sustainability
title: Olympic Games Sustainability Calculator
desc: Use the Olympic Games sustainability calculator to find out how sustainable the Olympic Games are ecologically, socially, and economically.

c: Facts and figures for Paris 2024: ​  Summer Olympic Games​ ​  Total of 8.8 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,714 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 10 billion USD with an overrun rate of 115%. ​  Use of 35 sports venues with 5.7% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 1.75 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Beijing 2022: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 1.0 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,874 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 38.5 billion USD with an overrun rate of 149%. ​  Use of 12 sports venues with 50% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 1.36 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Tokyo 2020: ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 9 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 11,037 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 35 billion USD with an overrun rate of 139%. ​  Use of 42 sports venues with 20.5% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 2.3 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for PyeongChang 2018: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 1.1 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,833 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 15.4 billion USD with an overrun rate of 14%. ​  Use of 13 sports venues with 46% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 1.9 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Rio de Janeiro 2016: ​​* ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 6.2 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 11,238 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 13.3 billion USD with an overrun rate of 352%. ​  Use of 32 sports venues with 26% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.6 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Sochi 2014: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  More than 1 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,780 athletes participated.   Overall cost of 59.7 billion USD with an overrun rate of 289%. ​  Use of 11 sports venues with 100% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.3 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for London 2012: ​​*   Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 8.2 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,568 athletes participated.   Overall cost of 13.3 billion USD with an overrun rate of 76%. ​  Use of 28 sports venues with 17.6% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.4 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Vancouver 2010: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 1.5 million visitors. ‍  Up to 2,536 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 8.9 billion USD with an overrun rate of 13%. ​  Use of 12 sports venues with 44.4% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.1 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Beijing 2008: ​​* ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 6.5 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,942 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 52.7 billion USD with an overrun rate of 2%. ​  Use of 31 sports venues with 32% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.9 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Torino 2006: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 0.9 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,494 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 5.3 billion USD with an overrun rate of 80%. ​  Use of 15 sports venues with 46.2% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 2.5 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Athens 2004: ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 3.8 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,625 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 18.7 billion USD with an overrun rate of 49%. ​​  Use of 35 sports venues with 26% of newly built or renovated facilities.   Generated 3.5 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Salt Lake City 2002: ​  Winter Olympic Games   Total of 1.5 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,402 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 2.9 billion USD with an overrun rate of 24%. ​​  Use of 10 sports venues with 11% of newly built or renovated facilities.  Generated 1.9 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Sydney 2000: ​* ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 6.7 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,651 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 8.1 billion USD with an overrun rate of 90%. ​  Use of 30 sports venues with 38% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 3.3 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Nagano 1998: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 1.3 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 2,180 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 17.9 billion USD with an overrun rate of 56%. ​  Use of 14 sports venues with 64.3% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 2.1 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Atlanta 1996: ​* ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 8.3 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 10,318 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 4.2 billion USD with an overrun rate of 151%. ​​  Use of 29 sports venues with 36.4% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​  Generated 2.7 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Lillehammer 1994: ​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 1.2 million visitors. ‍​  Up to 1,738 athletes participated. ​  Overall cost of 1.1 billion USD with an overrun rate of 277%. ​  Use of 10 sports venues with 80% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​ Generated 2 Mt CO2 eq.

Facts and figures for Barcelona 1992: ​* ​  Summer Olympic Games ​  Total of 3 million visitors. ‍​​  Up to 9,356 athletes participated. ​​  Overall cost of 9.3 billion USD with an overrun rate of 266%. ​  Use of 43 sports venues with 45.5% of newly built or renovated facilities.

Facts and figures for Albertville 1992: ​​​  Winter Olympic Games ​  Total of 0.9 million visitors. ‍​​  Up to 1,801 athletes participated. ​​  Overall cost of 2 billion USD with an overrun rate of 137%. ​  Use of 13 sports venues with 50% of newly built or renovated facilities. ​​  Generated 1.6 Mt CO2 eq.

Why not roast some chestnuts over a roaring winter fire, made from your tree? Some CO2 is still being produced, though. Why not try building a tree out of things you already own?

title: 0-60 Calculator
desc: Our 0-60 calculator gives you a fast and easy estimate of your car's acceleration time from 0 to 60 mph. It can also account for the type of car, type of tires, and road conditions.

m.h: Power output of the engine or the motor

name: 45 day
title: 45 Day Calculator
desc: This 45 day calculator helps in finding out 45 days from any given date.

c: Onim Example 1: What date is 45 days from December 20, 2024?
Onim Example 2: What is the date 45 days before August 1, 2025?

m.h: Including start date, not including end date. To include end date, check the box "Include end date".
Choose a date from the calendar.

c: How the result is calculated: Subtract the current date from 31 to find the days left in December: 31 - 20 = 11; Subtract the result from 45: 34; Subtract the last result from 31, corresponding to January: 34 - 31 = 3; Count the final days in February and write the final date: February 3, 2025.

How the result is calculated: Take one day from 45 corresponding to August 1st: 44; Subtract the last result from 31, corresponding to July: 44 - 31 = 13; Subtract the remaining days from 30, corresponding to June: 30 - 13 = 17; Write the final date: June 17, 2025.
Check our examples: Example 1 ⧉ — 45 days from December 20, 2024 Example 2 ⧉ — 45 days before August 01, 2025

Congratulations, you are a spoon!  Your hips are much wider than the bust. We recommend wearing bikinis that draw attention to the waist and de-emphasize the tummy area.
Congratulations, you are a triangle!  Your upper body is very slim, while the hips are ample. We recommend wearing bikinis that add volume to the upper body and show off your flat belly.
Congratulations, you are an inverted triangle!  You have an ample bust and slim hips. We recommend wearing bikinis with simple tops and accentuated bottoms.

Congratulations, you are a rectangle!  Your silhouette is proportional, but your waist is not clearly defined. We recommend wearing bikinis that are form-fitting around the waist, and add volume to the upper and lower body.
